text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batching throughput cliff detected across eu-west-1 serving fleet. p95 token latency > 6s, error-rate increased. PagerDuty triggered to oncall: maya

maya: seeing a hard drop in q_served and queue length spiking on the cb queues. KV cache hit-rate for model-rev 'redwood-3b-v1' fell from 91% -> 12% in the last 2m. Possibly cache blowout + microbatch pileup.

olivia: confirming, logs show repeated KV cache re-population storms: clients sending lots of short prefixes, cache entries thrashing. stack: 
```
2026-03-15T17:34:12Z srv-101 cb_engine: enqueue req id=abc123 len=8 microbatch_size=1
2026-03-15T17:34:12Z kvstore: evict model=redwood-3b-v1 key=kv_0x7f... reason=ttl_expire
2026-03-15T17:34:12Z cb_engine: batch_flush size=128 latency=1.2s
2026-03-15T17:34:13Z cb_engine: flush_error: queue_overflow
```

ram: initial mitigation idea: reduce `continuous_batch.max_inflight` and lower `microbatch.target_tokens`, re-enable per-tenant prefix throttling. We should also toggle `kv_cache.soft_evict=true` to avoid full-thrash.

maya: agreed. I'm going to push a hotfix to reduce concurrency on the problematic shard group and enable jitter on batch flush. Rolling change now to one host pool (canary):
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/srv/configs/apply" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"scope":"eu-west-1:pool-7","continuous_batch.max_inflight":64,"microbatch.target_tokens":32,"continuous_batch.enable_jitter":true}'
```

anna: tagging runbook: https://internal/runbooks/continuous-batching (see section 3.2 - kv-cache thrash). Also notifying Support with customer impact note.

sre-bot: Canary update succeeded on 4/4 hosts in pool-7. Observability: p95 latency down 45% on canary, kv hit-rate stabilized ~78%.

olivia: good signal. However global queue backlog still high because other pools are still on old config. We should do a staged rollout with 2-min pause and monitor evictions.

maya: starting staged rollout to remaining eu-west-1 pools. Policy: +1 pool every 90s, abort if error-rate > 5% or 30s sustained p95 above 5s.

support-bot: creating status page draft: "We're investigating increased latencies affecting text-generation in EU. Mitigation in progress; some requests may see delays or errors." Ticket opened: INC-2026-1983 (customer-facing).

ram: quick note on root cause hypothesis: customer traffic pattern changed to many tiny prompts causing K and V cache entries to be written for many distinct prefixes. Continuous batching was grouping too aggressively (large max_inflight) which amplified kv eviction churn and microbatches kept flushing tiny jobs -> throughput cliff. Need longer-term: adaptively shrink group window for low token-length workloads and prioritize cache-preserved lanes.

olivia: agree. Short-term we're also going to set `kv_cache.max_entries_per_model` to 50k from 200k for redwood-3b-v1 to limit memory pressure while we stabilize. Applying now to eu-west-1 only.

maya: rollout complete across eu-west-1 at 17:39Z. Metrics: global p95 latency down to 1.6s (from 6.4s), error-rate reduced to baseline. KV hit-rate climbing back to ~80% within 3m.

anna: customer impact summary for handoff: ~12 minutes of elevated errors for a subset of customers (regions: eu-west-1). Top impacted customers: cust-42 (realtime chat), cust-117 (batch embeddings) — both flagged for follow-up. No data exposure. Root cause suspected config + traffic pattern; hotfix applied and rolled back staged across pools.

ram: perf cliff indicators we logged: sustained microbatch size avg=1.1 tokens (should be 8-32), queue length per-worker peaked at 9k, KV store write rate spiked x8, GC activity high. Dump of metrics snapshot: 
```
metric:continuous_batch.microbatch_avg_tokens 1.1
metric:continuous_batch.max_inflight_before 256
metric:kv_cache.hit_rate 0.12 -> 0.8
metric:worker.queue_len p95 9200
metric:errors.request_timeout 241
```

olivia: added follow-up work items to infra board: adaptive microbatch heuristics, per-tenant slow-path to avoid cache churn, alert refinement for kv hit-rate drop.

maya: paging note: I'll handoff to ram for overnight. Ram, I'm oncall-swapped at 18:00Z; please pick this up and monitor eu-west for 2 hours. Key actions: monitor p95, kv_hit_rate, and error spikes; abort rollout if anything regresses; coordinate with support to update customers.

ram: ack. I'll maintain the mitigation knobs: `continuous_batch.max_inflight`, `microbatch.target_tokens`, `kv_cache.max_entries_per_model`, and `continuous_batch.enable_jitter`. Handoff checklist completed.

support-bot: support notified customers cust-42 & cust-117; follow-up ticket created and owners assigned.

maya: leaving notes in incident doc: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-1983, include the config diffs and metric snapshots. Will create postmortem starter after stabilization. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Post-rollback audit log:
```
2026-03-15T17:40:01Z config:apply user=maya scope=eu-west-1:pool-7 key=continuous_batch.max_inflight old=256 new=64
2026-03-15T17:40:01Z config:apply user=maya scope=eu-west-1:pool-7 key=microbatch.target_tokens old=128 new=32
2026-03-15T17:41:50Z config:apply user=olivia scope=eu-west-1 key=kv_cache.max_entries_per_model old=200000 new=50000
```

ram: will follow up with a brief RCA draft in the morning. For now, mitigation stands and system health is back to acceptable levels. I'll keep the thread updated if anything changes.

incident-bot: Incident cleared from page-after state; manual close pending.

maya: thanks team. Good catch on the kv thrash pattern. We'll take the larger product/infra work into next sprint.
